body:
Gold is trading in record territory, and that context explains why every strike on the board looks unusually high. Spot XAU/USD is quoted around $4,397 today, the current XAU/USD exchange rate is 4,397.50, with a previous close of 4,376.59, and the metal has been grinding higher after a strong jobs-data reaction, gold gained over 2.30% in the day and more than 7% in the week after US jobs data was mixed, with a softer Nonfarm Payrolls print. That rally is why Kalshi's above ladder for August 31, 2026 crosses 50/50 near the $4,411.99 strike, and why Polymarket's weekly touch-high contracts for $4,450–$4,600 are trading with real value instead of sitting near zero — the market is pricing spot already close to those levels, not assigning them fat tail odds.

The scanner flagged one small ladder opportunity on Polymarket: buying YES on hit low $4,250 at 1.1¢ and NO on hit low $4,200 at 98¢ for the week of August 17, 2026, a combined cost of 99.1¢ for a payout that's effectively guaranteed to be $1 (touching the deeper $4,200 low logically requires having first passed through $4,250). The edge is real but tiny — under a penny per contract, capped at 36 contracts, for about $0.32 total. That's a textbook thin-book artifact: these are deep, low-volume strike rungs on a touch-market ladder, and someone would need to clear both legs simultaneously to capture it, so it's a curiosity rather than a meaningful mispricing.

Otherwise it's a quiet day. Kalshi's settle-style year-end and month-end gold brackets and Polymarket's touch-high/touch-low contracts are moving in line with each other and with spot, the Aug 18 up/down coin-flip contract sits at 49/51 as you'd expect, and no other cross-platform edges cleared the scanner's fee and liquidity filters.
headline: Gold's record run keeps strikes elevated; only a sub-penny Polymarket ladder quirk stands out
